caption: Luke closely links Jesus with God’s Son, David’s throne and an endless kingdom. It is a strong Christian fulfilment claim, while Chronicles first points to Solomon.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Chronicles predict Jesus’s reign? God promises David’s son an enduring throne and calls him His son. Luke applies the same cluster of ideas to Jesus.
slides.body: God promises David’s son an enduring throne and calls him His son. Luke applies the same cluster of ideas to Jesus.
slides.heading: Did Chronicles predict Jesus’s reign?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of 1Chr 17:12-13: I will establish his throne forever. I will be his Father, and he will be My son.
slides.body: I will establish his throne forever. I will be his Father, and he will be My son.
slides.heading: 1Chr 17:12-13

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Lk 1:32–33, BSB: The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David, and He will reign forever. His kingdom will never end!
slides.body: The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David, and He will reign forever. His kingdom will never end!
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Lk 1:32–33

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Luke’s connection is unusually close Luke says Jesus will receive David’s throne, be called God’s Son and rule forever.
slides.body: Luke says Jesus will receive David’s throne, be called God’s Son and rule forever.
slides.heading: Luke’s connection is unusually close

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Solomon still comes first The promised son builds the temple, which Solomon does. Luke presents Jesus as the dynasty’s enduring culmination.
slides.body: The promised son builds the temple, which Solomon does. Luke presents Jesus as the dynasty’s enduring culmination.
slides.heading: But Solomon still comes first

title: David's throne forever
